---
title: "Verde River fish: a community linked by total biomass"
author: "Simon Frost"
engine: julia
---

```{julia}
#| output: false
ENV["GKSwstype"] = "100"
using MatrixCommunityModels
using MatrixProjectionModels: lambda
using Plots, Printf
```

## The model

Rogosch et al. (2019) modelled seven fish species of the Verde River, Arizona: three
natives (*Catostomus clarkii* CACL, *Gila robusta* GIRO, *Catostomus insignis* CAIN) and
four non-natives (*Lepomis cyanellus* LECY, *Micropterus dolomieu* MIDO, *Cyprinella
lutrensis* CYLU, *Ameiurus natalis* AMNA). Each species has three stages and its state is
biomass in grams. Survival depends on the kind of year (spring flood, summer flood,
medium flood, drought, or none of these). The species are linked by one **dependency
assumption**: the fecundity of every species is multiplied by `max(0, 1 - B/K)`, where
`B` is the total biomass of all fish and `K` = 47,660 g.

`verde_fish_model()` builds this community from the published vital-rate tables. Its
source in `src/models.jl` is short: three survival transitions and one to three
fecundity transitions per species, and one line saying that every stage occupies the
`biomass` pool gram for gram.

```{julia}
m = verde_fish_model()
fish = m.community
```

```{julia}
[(t.name, t.from => t.to, t.kind) for t in species(fish, :CYLU).transitions]
```

## Projection through the 1964-2017 flow record

Each year's environment is its set of year-type flags.

```{julia}
m.years[1:3], m.envs[1:3]
```

```{julia}
sol = project(fish, m.n0, m.envs)
```

Rogosch et al. report relative abundance of the two older stages. Biomass converts to
numbers through the individuals-per-gram of each stage.

```{julia}
adults = reduce(hcat, [sol[sp][:, 2] .* m.density[sp][2] .+ sol[sp][:, 3] .* m.density[sp][3]
                       for sp in species_names(fish)])
rel = adults ./ sum(adults; dims = 2)
yrs = [m.years; m.years[end] + 1]
plot(yrs[2:end], rel[2:end, :]; label = permutedims(String.(species_names(fish))),
     xlabel = "Year", ylabel = "Relative abundance (stages 2 and 3)", lw = 2, legend = :outerright)
```

## Agreement with the original R code

`test/reference/fish_det_biomass.csv` was produced by the authors' R script, run with the
same flow record and the initial biomass of the vital-rate table (see
`test/reference/R/run_fish_reference.R`). Each of its rows is the state before that
year's update.

```{julia}
ref_file = joinpath(pkgdir(MatrixCommunityModels), "test", "reference", "fish_det_biomass.csv")
ref = permutedims(reduce(hcat, [parse.(Float64, split(l, ",")[2:end]) for l in readlines(ref_file)[2:end]]))
got = sol.u[1:54, :]
(identical = count(got .== ref), of = length(ref), max_abs_difference = maximum(abs.(got .- ref)))
```

All 1134 values (54 years, 21 states) are identical to the last bit.

## What the pool does

Total biomass, the only thing the species share, stays below `K`:

```{julia}
plot(m.years, sol.pools[1:end-1, 1]; label = "total biomass", xlabel = "Year", ylabel = "g", lw = 2)
hline!([47660]; label = "K", ls = :dash)
```

Freezing a species at a year type and a biomass gives an ordinary projection matrix, so
its growth rate in that situation can be read off. Here each species alone in an almost
empty river, by year type:

```{julia}
flags(; kw...) = merge((SP_highflood = 0, SU_highflood = 0, medflood = 0, drought = 0, nonevent = 0), kw)
types = ["spring flood" => flags(SP_highflood = 1), "summer flood" => flags(SU_highflood = 1),
         "medium flood" => flags(medflood = 1), "drought" => flags(drought = 1),
         "non-event" => flags(nonevent = 1)]
for sp in species(fish)
    lams = [lambda(lower(sp, Context(zeros(3), (biomass = 0.0,), env))) for (_, env) in types]
    @printf("%-5s %s\n", sp.name, join([@sprintf("%-13s %5.2f", first(t), l) for (t, l) in zip(types, lams)], "  "))
end
```

The natives (CACL, GIRO, CAIN) do best after spring floods and decline in droughts; the
non-natives do best in droughts and non-event years. That is the autecology the model was
given. Competition appears only when the
community is put together.

## Asking a new question takes one line

Because the community is a composite, changing its membership is a matter of composing a
different set of species. The natives without the non-natives:

```{julia}
natives = community((species(fish, s) for s in (:CACL, :GIRO, :CAIN))...)
n0 = [p for p in m.n0 if p.first in (:CACL, :GIRO, :CAIN)]
alone = project(natives, n0, m.envs)
plot(yrs, [sum(sol[:CACL]; dims = 2) sum(alone[:CACL]; dims = 2)];
     label = ["CACL, full community" "CACL, natives only"], xlabel = "Year", ylabel = "Biomass (g)", lw = 2)
```

## Reference

Rogosch, J. S., Tonkin, J. D., Lytle, D. A., Merritt, D. M., Reynolds, L. V. & Olden,
J. D. (2019). Increasing drought favors nonnative fishes in a dryland river: evidence
from a multispecies demographic model. *Ecosphere* 10, e02681. Code and data:
<https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.1309024> (MIT licence).
